added_failures_note: derived from the reviewed run's own arms. baseline_suite at 4d5c4389 (base-arm.log, extracted tree on all_debug) ran tests/test_a_phase_transition_is_published_before_review_duties.py and tests/test_staged_write_inventory.py: 50 passed, 2 errors, EXIT=1, the errors being the staged-write cases whose setup shells out to git in a tree that is not a repository. after_suite at a3989001ca (head-arm.log, same extraction) ran the same files plus the node's own test: 51 passed, the same 2 errors, EXIT=1. The two failure ids are identical in both arms and are attributed to collection scaffolding, so the added set is empty and the base-to-head delta is exactly the node's own passing case.

0.reason: a test fixture's sweep stub has the wrong signature, so the test station logs sweep failures it ignores; the derivation and transition assertions are unaffected

findings.text: _Sweeps.__call__(self) takes no arguments but SweepBeat._run calls the sweep with (project, session=..., now=..., writer=...), so every sweep this test's station requests raises TypeError and is logged as station-sweep-failure (visible twice in the captured stderr of the negative-control log); the case still passes because it asserts on transition rows, so the sweep arm of the station under test is never exercised and any future sweep assertion here would measure a stub that never runs. The sibling file's stub at tests/test_a_phase_transition_is_published_before_review_duties.py:82 carries the correct keyword signature and is the form to copy.

assert not release.is_set() cannot fail, because the only release.set() in the file is in the finally that runs after this line, so the claim it names is carried entirely by the transition assertion above it; an assertion that cannot name a condition under which it reddens is not coverage of the claim it names.

the comment justifies the worker's own store connection with 'a store handle is bound to the thread that opened it', but the store connects with check_same_thread=False at reckon/crew/station_store.py:379, so no such binding exists; the separate connection is still reasonable, and the wrong reason is repeated in docs/evidence/fragments/the-monitor-reads-each-fact-once/review-duties-are-derived-off-the-tick-thread.html, where a reader will take it as fact.

the commit barrier this repair added has no assertion that fails if it is reverted, because nothing holds DutyBeat.committing() open and asserts that a requested derivation does not enter publish; the ordering case instead waits for in_flight() to empty at tests/test_a_phase_transition_is_published_before_review_duties.py:178-183, so removing self._await_committed() would leave every test green.

DutyBeat repeats SweepBeat's off-tick single-flight scaffolding at reckon/crew/station.py:298 (in-flight set, one pending request kept for the next pass, error-catch-and-continue loop) rather than extracting it, and it drops the injectable start seam both SweepBeat and ReflexBeat expose, which is why its own test has to drive real threads and timing events instead of a synchronous start callable.
